title: Constant-time RFC 4648 Base64 block decoder (256 chars -> 192 bytes)
contract_header:
use spec = "rvp5rdmmqprcrnoonholzl5ui74mpffwfy7mhsnrplhuo46dgnkq"  // ct_base64_decode_spec.ode

fn ct_base64_decode(out: 192 bytes, src: n bytes, n: number)
    requires no_overlap(out, src)
    requires n >= 256
    requires n <= 256
    ensures out = spec.b64_decode(src)
    returns spec.b64_valid(src)
    trace depends on n
    stack 64
task_summary: Implement `ct_base64_decode(out, src, n)`, a constant-time RFC 4648 Standard Base64 block decoder that decodes 256 input characters in `src` into 192 output bytes in `out` (`ensures out = spec.b64_decode(src)`) and returns `1` if every byte of `src` is a valid Standard Base64 character (`'A'..'Z'`, `'a'..'z'`, `'0'..'9'`, `'+'`, `'/'`) or `0` otherwise (`returns spec.b64_valid(src)`). Because `trace depends on n` excludes every byte of `src` from the execution trace, neither control flow nor memory addresses may depend on any input byte — use branchless arithmetic or hardware conditional select (`cmov*` on x86-64, `csel` on AArch64) instead of branches or byte-indexed lookup tables. Your goal is BOTH full verification (`shown`) AND maximum decoding throughput (lowest cycles per 256-byte block).
opt_goal: reduce total cycles per 256-byte block (loop cyc/iter and cyc/B) by removing call overhead, shortening critical dependency chains, or unrolling/interleaving while preserving full verification (`shown`) and strict constant-time trace exclusion (`trace depends on n`)
